survey: A black clay-style cat sits upright on a wooden tabletop in front of a wall with vertical orange stripes. The camera is a little above the cat and sees it in three-quarter view from the front-left. Body: a rounded pear shape resting on its haunches. The two front paws sit on the planks and their tops are slightly visible, which fits the raised camera. The tail curls forward along the tabletop and lies flat on it, and the soft shadow falls to the right on the same plane, so contact is sound. Head: sits on the body and is turned toward the viewer's left. The nose is off-center to the left, and the right-hand ear is seen broader and more side-on, both of which fit that turn. Collar: a red ring around the neck whose front arc dips lower than its sides, as a horizontal ring seen from slightly above should. Tabletop: the plank seams run diagonally back to the right and the back edge meets the wall. The planks are only mildly foreshortened, which is acceptable stylization and agrees with the raised camera. Wall: the stripes stay vertical, matching an untilted view.

errors.where: Cat's eyes, especially the far eye on the viewer's left
errors.what: The head is turned to the viewer's left, as the off-center nose and the ears show, but both eyes are drawn as full, front-facing circles of about the same size. The far eye even bulges out past the outline of the head. On a turned head the far eye should be narrower and partly tucked behind the curve of the face. Drawn this way, the eyes look pasted on flat rather than wrapping around the head.

fix: Keep the cat's head turned slightly to the left in three-quarter view, with both eyes following the curve of the head. The near eye (viewer's right) is a full round shape. The far eye (viewer's left) is narrower and slightly smaller, tucked inside the edge of the head and partly hidden by the cheek, not sticking out past the head's outline.
